surprises.description: Adjusted diluted EPS was expected to decline 3%–5% year over year, but instead increased almost 4%. The result reversed the expected direction by roughly 7–9 percentage points.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Diluted EPS as adjusted increased almost 4% in the quarter.”

surprises.description: Same-facility adjusted admissions grew 3%, above the preview’s 1.7%–1.9% consensus estimate. This was a stronger volume result than expected.

HCA raised its 2026 Medicaid Supplemental Payment net-benefit guidance to $600–800 million, up from the preview’s $300–500 million assumption. The increase was supported by $650 million recognized year-to-date, including an incremental $50 million in Q3.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised its 2026 Medicaid Supplemental Payment net benefit guidance to $600-800 million”; it recognized “$50 million incremental in Q3 and $650 million year-to-date through September.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Guidance assumes $300–500M net benefit for FY2026”; the preview also flagged a “$100–300M headwind in 2H.”

surprises.description: Management said 2026 results should land in the upper half of guidance, more favorable than the preview’s base case of a narrowed range around $29.00–30.00 and its view that lifting the low end was needed. The call facts do not provide a revised range or exact EPS figure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management expects full-year 2026 results to land in the upper half of guidance ranges.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected “the FY range narrowed to ~$29.00–30.00”; it said “low-end raise required” versus $29.45 consensus.

surprises.description: Exchange equivalent admissions fell about 19% year over year, worse than the 15%–16% decline the preview described as the current run rate. The roughly 3–4 percentage-point deeper decline was partly offset by sequential improvement from Q2.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Exchange equivalent admissions declined approximately 19% year-over-year (worse than the 15-16% guided) but showed sequential improvement of about 8% from Q2 to Q3 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged exchange-sourced adjusted admissions at “−15%” and described the “~15% run-rate.”

surprises.description: The exchange-to-uninsured shift had a substantial quantified quarterly cost: management estimated an approximately $400 million unfavorable adjusted EBITDA impact, with uninsured at 10.5% of equivalent admissions. The preview highlighted the migration to uninsured but did not anticipate or quantify this quarterly impact.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The payer mix shift from exchanges to uninsured caused an estimated unfavorable adjusted EBITDA impact of roughly $400 million in the quarter, with uninsured rising to 10.5% of equivalent admissions versus 8.5% a year earlier.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said exchange losers had migrated “almost one for one to uninsured” and flagged the FY exchange headwind at “$(1.0–1.2)B,” but gave no quarterly EBITDA-impact estimate.

surprises.description: Outpatient surgeries fell 3.7%, considerably weaker than the preview’s consensus expectation for outpatient cases to decline 1.3%. Inpatient surgeries fell 1.4%, less weak than the recent Q2 inpatient decline of 2.3% cited in the preview, so the surgery picture was mixed.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Inpatient surgeries fell 1.4% and outpatient surgeries fell 3.7% (ASC surgeries down 5.4%, HOPD down 2.9%).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “Consensus models outpatient cases −1.3%” and cited Q2 inpatient surgery at “−2.3%.”

surprises.description: Same-facility cost per equivalent admission improved 40 basis points sequentially, better than the preview’s cited 1.4% sequential decrease. The year-over-year result was essentially flat, as expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Same-facility cost per equivalent admission (excluding supplemental payments) was essentially flat year-over-year and improved 40 basis points sequentially.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said cost per equivalent admission “was essentially flat YoY ex-supplemental payments, −1.4% sequentially.”

surprises.description: Professional fees rose about 12% year over year, faster than the preview’s cited growth rate of about 8.5%. Management attributed the increase to radiology and anesthesiology.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Professional fees rose about 12% year-over-year, driven by radiology and anesthesiology.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “Professional fees still growing ~8.5% (anesthesia, radiology).”

surprises.description: Management gave a 2027 earnings outlook on this call, although the preview said HCA did not guide 2027 until January, and said earnings should be generally consistent with 2026. That is a firmer and more reassuring outlook than the preview’s expected cautious or limited framing, despite a material payment headwind.
surprises.fact_evidence: “For 2027, management expects earnings to be generally consistent with 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “HCA does not guide 2027 until January, so the call Q&A is the entire event”; the preview also described “cautious 2027 framing” as a bear-case signal.

surprises.description: Management quantified a $550–650 million reduction in 2027 Medicaid Supplemental Payments tied to prior-year grandfathered approvals. The preview discussed 2026 payment laps and 2027 renewal risk, but did not anticipate this specific 2027 reduction.
surprises.fact_evidence: “For 2027, management expects earnings to be generally consistent with 2026, pressured by $550-650 million less in Medicaid Supplemental Payments tied to prior-year grandfathered approvals.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged the “2H $100–300M lap headwind plus renewal risk” but did not state a 2027 reduction estimate.

surprises.description: HCA repurchased approximately $3 billion of shares in Q3 and said it planned to complete most of its existing authorization by year-end. The preview noted the $2.1 billion Q2 repurchase but did not set an expectation for Q3 buybacks or for completing the authorization so soon.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company deployed significant capital in Q3, repurchasing approximately $3 billion of shares”; it had “plans to complete most of the existing buyback authorization by year-end.”
